correctness.rationale: For each board, row/column coverage is a necessary and sufficient domination criterion. Two function layers and their permutation overlap exhaust every optimum. Degrees follow from \(n-1\)-image cross edges and exact multiplicity. The radius n follows from disjoint same-layer targets and permutation centers. For cross-layer distances, a uniformly random bridge permutation has mean overlap 2; if none attains 3, vanishing 2x2 assignment differences force the two functions to be constant for \(n\ge3\). A direct cross-layer bridge then attains \(2n-3\), and coordinate-support counts lower-bound the extremal pair by \(2n-3\). Both checkers independently reconstructed the finite graphs; no general claim is inferred solely from finite cases.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General existence, connectedness or cograph diameter claims do not determine the present square rook exchange metric; the rook graph for \(n\ge3\) has an induced four-vertex path and is not a cograph. Add/delete reconfiguration with a spare vertex is not the same graph.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary material establishes the reconfiguration models, general gamma-graph facts and known enumeration of rook dominating placements, but does not give the sharp jump exchange radius and diameter or the degree strata for square boards. In particular, the exact count \(2n^n-n!\) is explicitly credited to prior literature. Relevant accessible earlier claims are not logically equivalent; priority risk from unindexed chessboard/edge-domination literature remains.
residual_risks: An exact gamma-graph calculation might exist in unindexed chessboard, edge-domination, or earlier unpublished literature.
Neither an external scholarly audit nor a comprehensive search of every older paper has been performed.

value.rationale: The complete minimum-rook-domination exchange geometry on arbitrary rectangles is a motivated all-parameter classification: the balanced board creates a second Hamming layer and new direct shortcuts, causing a sharp diameter shift and three local degree strata. This captures the exact feasible cost of preserving minimum domination under one-for-one replacement, a feature not implied by the classical minimum-rook count or general model definitions. The result is not an arbitrary finite slice.
